definitions.explanation: Bacteria or microorganisms that cause disease. Used in medical, scientific, and everyday contexts when talking about the source of infections.

examples.japanese: {病原菌|びょうげんきん}が{検出|けんしゅつ}された。
{手洗|てあら}いで{病原菌|びょうげんきん}の{感染|かんせん}を{防|ふせ}ぐことができる。
examples.english: You can prevent the spread of germs by washing your hands.

examples.japanese: {研究者|けんきゅうしゃ}たちは{新|あたら}しい{病原菌|びょうげんきん}の{特定|とくてい}に{成功|せいこう}し、{治療法|ちりょうほう}の{開発|かいはつ}に{取|と}り{組|く}んでいる。
examples.english: Researchers succeeded in identifying a new pathogen and are working on developing a treatment.

notes:
A common word in health and science contexts. Though technically {菌|きん} refers to bacteria/fungi, in everyday Japanese {病原菌|びょうげんきん} is used loosely to mean any disease-causing microorganism, including viruses.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {病原菌|びょうげんきん}を{除去|じょきょ}する: to remove pathogens
- {病原菌|びょうげんきん}の{感染|かんせん}: infection by pathogens
- {病原菌|びょうげんきん}が{繁殖|はんしょく}する: pathogens multiply
- {病原菌|びょうげんきん}を{持|も}つ: to carry pathogens

RELATED TERMS:
- {細菌|さいきん}: bacteria — broader term for all bacteria
- ウイルス: virus — technically distinct from bacteria
- {病原体|びょうげんたい}: pathogen — more precise scientific term covering all disease-causing agents

FORMATION:
{病原|びょうげん} (disease-causing) + {菌|きん} (bacteria/germ)
